subject: blueprintSpitfire
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: Spitfire fighter plane.
Style: cyanotype blueprint.
reasoning:
I'm thinking through a Spitfire design in cyanotype blueprint style, planning a deep blue and white palette with grid lines and technical drawing elements, treating it as a static model without joints.

For geometry I'll loft the fuselage along the z-axis, extrude elliptical wings, and add the tail, propeller, canopy, radiator, landing gear, exhaust stacks, and roundel decals using SVG for the concentric circles plus text annotations.

I'm working out the real-world proportions -- wingspan 11.2m, length 9.1m, height 3.9m tail-down -- and figuring out the nose-up stance so the propeller clears the ground, positioning the fuselage axis sloping from nose to tail with wheels and tail wheel placed to keep everything grounded correctly.

Now I'm setting fuselage cross-section stations along z from the spinner tip back to the tail, defining width and height at each point for the loft, and planning the paint function to render a blueprint-style base color with grid lines that brighten along edges based on surface normal and position.

For the wings, I'm working out the extrusion axes so the outline's span maps to x and the chord direction maps to z, computing the leading and trailing edge curves as elliptical functions of x to get that classic Spitfire wing shape.

Now I'm positioning the landing gear legs and wheels under the wing, then starting on the vertical tail fin.

Adding a canopy sphere with frame rods, then working out the propeller blades as rotated extrusions around the spinner axis with a curved blade outline.

For the spinner I'm lathing a tapered cone profile around the z-axis near the nose, and positioning exhaust stacks as small cylinders along each side of the cowl.

Now I'm adding radiator scoops under the wings as boxes, plus rod-shaped machine guns and cannons projecting forward from the wing leading edges, and placing roundel decals as flat planes on the wing tops and fuselage sides for the blueprint-style markings.

For the fuselage roundels, I decide to use a decal projection onto the surface rather than calculating exact width offsets, which is more reliable given the tapering fuselage shape. I'm also planning text decals for the aircraft markings and dimension-line callouts above the wings to complete the blueprint aesthetic.

I'll skip ground-level annotations and focus the dimension arrows and glow effects on the wing surfaces and canopy frame instead, giving the blueprint lines a light cyan glow. Now I'm defining a paint helper function for the wing surfaces that uses the surface normal to blend lighting and color based on height.

Still writing paint logic...

I'm adding the tail wheel geometry with its strut, sizing the main wheels with lighter hub disks against dark tires, then defining a wing planform function that computes leading and trailing edge curves based on span and chord for the tail plane.

I'm now dimensioning the main wing (span 5.6, chord 2.3) and checking its vertical placement relative to the fuselage, then setting up the tailplane's span, chord, offset, and thickness similarly.

Skipping elevators for now, I'm sketching the fin's outline at the rear of the fuselage with leading and trailing edge points defining a swept shape, including a rough rudder section.

Adjusting rudder outline coordinates to overlap the fin trailing edge with slightly thicker strokes. For the canopy, I'm positioning a scaled sphere above the fuselage top near the tail station, with a rear fairing and windscreen to follow.

Still shaping the canopy frame...

I should also add a small antenna mast near the cockpit, a fuselage code label like "KL-X", and blueprint-style annotation arrows with measurements on the wing to give it that technical drawing feel.

I'll just accept the orientation ambiguity and move forward rather than overthink the exact axis mapping. For the roundel design, I'm sketching concentric circles with white outline strokes at decreasing radii, leaving transparent gaps between rings to suggest the classic insignia look.

Now I'm adding the fin stripe details and panel rivet lines to the wings, then setting up helper functions for mirroring parts across the fuselage. Writing gun and cannon geometry as thin rods at specific wing positions, followed by exhaust stack placement along the cowl using small angled cylinders in a dark bluish color...

Working out the exhaust stack curve positions and chin radiator scoop geometry...

Checking overall model proportions: fin height, prop clearance, and tail wheel ground contact all seem consistent. Now figuring out prop blade placement with rotated extrusions spaced 120° apart with a slight offset angle.

Confirming the wheel cylinders orient along the x-axis correctly, and double-checking lathe/extrude coordinate conventions before writing the final module.
